subject: Milestone plan & billing guardrails — Acme Health MAP
messages:
From: Sara Connors <sara.connors@acmehealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Initial MAP + commercial questions

Hi Kimberly / Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with throughput and the latency profiles. Procurement asked me to pull together a mutual action plan (MAP) so we can align the evaluation milestones and the commercial commitments. I've attached our starting MAP (MAP_v1.xlsx).

A few commercial points procurement wants cleared before we move to contracting:
- How do pricing discounts map to ramp milestones? We need a clear schedule (e.g., X% discount at 30/60/90 days or spend thresholds).
- True-up cadence: procurement favors monthly true-ups to reconcile usage vs committed spend.
- Price protection: they want a locked price window during initial procurement cycle (they mentioned 24 months).
- Usage definition: what counts as billable tokens — do cached/prefetched tokens or internal test runs count?

Can you propose a commercial scaffolding that ties MAP milestones to pricing and commit ramps? We'd like to review redlines in parallel with technical eval to avoid last-minute surprises.

We can do a 60-minute alignment next week — propose Tue/Thu morning.

Thanks,
Sara Connors
Head of AI Programs
Acme Health
(attachment: MAP_v1.xlsx)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sara Connors <sara.connors@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial MAP + commercial questions

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Copying Marcus since he'll help with the technical gating and ramp assumptions.

High level proposal (we'll formalize in the MAP_v2 attachment):
- Ramp milestones: 30/60/90 day checkpoints tied to validated traffic (we recommend measuring committed ramp against 95th-percentile sustained QPS over 7 days, to avoid transient spikes).
- Discount schedule: tiered discounts tied to committed monthly spend band (e.g., 0-50k tokens/month: base price; 50-200k: 7% off; 200k+: 15% off). Milestone attainment triggers the next tier.
- True-ups: standard is quarterly look-back true-ups with 30-day invoice window; we can be flexible to monthly true-ups during the initial 90-day eval if procurement requires.
- Price protection: we typically offer 12 months price protection from contract signature. If you need 24 months we'll escalate for approval; otherwise, propose 18 months as a middle ground.
- Usage definitions: billable units = tokens produced by hosted inference calls (generation + response tokens). We exclude cached prefix tokens served from a customer-managed cache; test sandbox tokens are excluded if marked with the sandbox flag in the API key. We'll put explicit definitions in the SOW.

I'll send a redlineable MAP_v2 and a short commercial_summary.pdf that maps milestones to financials. Proposed alignment call: Tue 16 Jun 10:00 PT or Thu 18 Jun 09:00 PT — let me know what works.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attachment: MAP_v2.xlsx) (attachment: commercial_summary.pdf)

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: redline items to watch (true-ups / usage defs)

Kim / Lauren / Rishi —
Following Kim's draft, I reviewed the commercial summary and suggested redlines from a technical operations POV. Main risks and suggested language:

1) Retroactive true-ups: procurement may request open retrospective true-ups. We should cap retroactive true-ups to a maximum of 10% of the billed amount per quarter and require we provide usage reports with 30 days to dispute. Suggested clause: "Customer may request adjustments for unaccounted usage for up to 90 days following the end of the billing period; Provider's liability for retrospective billing adjustments shall not exceed ten percent (10%) of the billed amount for the applicable billing period."

2) Usage definition clarity: the contract must enumerate what counts as billable (inference requests, tokens generated, embeddings, reranking). Exclude: pre-warmed cache hits (if cache is customer-managed), internal QA runs marked with sandbox flag, and system-initiated telemetry. We'll add a short table in the SOW.

3) Price protection: if we agree to >12 months we need explicit escalation authority documented for pricing changes tied to hardware cost variance. If procurement wants 24 months, legal should preserve an upward adjustment clause tied to published cloud GPU list price changes.

I'll prepare a redline for the MSA and the SOW that captures the cap language and a tighter usage def. If legal is okay, I recommend we push for quarterly true-ups with an optional monthly reconciliation during the first quarter of production.

Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
(attachment: suggested_contract_clauses.txt)

From: Sara Connors <sara.connors@acmehealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial MAP + commercial questions

Thanks Kim / Marcus — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few items from procurement and finance:
- Price protection: our preference is 24 months to match our internal budget cycle. 18 months is better than 12, but we'd prefer 24 if you can commit.
- True-up cadence: procurement really wants monthly true-ups for the first six months to avoid surprise spend; they are willing to move to quarterly thereafter.
- Ramp metric: we understand your 95th-percentile recommendation, but procurement wants peak sustained QPS for a 24-hour window as the gating metric for certain regulatory workloads. Can you confirm if Redwood can measure that and include in the SOW?
- Contracting timeline: procurement has a June 30 cutoff for budget approval to hit a July 1 purchase order. If we can get redlines and a DocuSign by Jun 24, procurement can process.

Attaching procurement requirements and the budget cadence doc. Happy to discuss on Tue morning.

Best,
Sara
(attachment: procurement_requirements.pdf)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sara Connors <sara.connors@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 16:35:00 -0700
Subject: Consolidated proposal + next steps (MAP final)

Sara / Procurement — thanks for the candid asks. After internal review with Marcus and Legal (Lauren), here is a consolidated position intended to unblock contracting while protecting both parties. I've attached MAP_final.xlsx with the milestone checklist and a draft redline to the SOW/MSA.

Key commercial compromises:
- Price protection: 18 months from signature with a 6-month scheduled review. If Acme requests an extension to 24 months, Redwood will consider it for a fee schedule adjustment tied to hardware cost indices (we can quantify in the redline).
- True-ups: Quarterly true-ups standard. During the initial 90 days of production we will provide monthly reconciliations (informational) and allow one monthly invoiced true-up on request. Retroactive billing adjustments are capped at 10% per quarter; disputes must be raised within 30 days of invoice.
- Ramp metric and measurement: Commitments will be validated against a 24-hour sustained peak QPS window for regulatory routes (as requested) and a 7-day 95th-percentile for consumer routes. We'll instrument monitoring dashboards and provide a signed report at each milestone.
- Usage definition: Billable = tokens produced by hosted inference API calls (generation + assistant response + embeddings + reranking). Excluded: customer-managed cache hits (explicit cache header), sandbox/test keys annotated as "sandbox", internal Redwood QA. Exact taxonomy is in the SOW.
- Discount schedule: milestone-triggered discounts tied to committed monthly spend bands (see attached table).

Operational notes and timeline:
- Requested items for DocuSign: final redlines to MSA + SOW by Wed 24 Jun to meet your Jun 30 procurement cutoff.
- Owners: Legal redline (Lauren) — finalize clauses; Finance/invoicing setup (Rishi) — prepare invoices and onboarding credit terms; Technical validation (Marcus) — confirm dashboard metrics and instrumentation.
- Production target: If contract signed by Jun 30 and P.O. issued, target production-ready on July 15 with phased ramp (30/60/90 day checkpoints).

Action items:
1) Lauren to push redline to Sara by Wed 24 Jun (owner: lauren_bishop)
2) Marcus to share metric instrumentation plan and sample dashboard by Tue 23 Jun (owner: marcus_lin)
3) Rishi to confirm invoicing cadence and set up billing profile by Wed 24 Jun (owner: rishi_malhotra)
4) Sara/Procurement to confirm acceptance of 18-month price protection or request escalation (owner: Acme)

If you agree to this position, we'll circulate DocuSign links and the final MAP checklist. Happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow to walk through the redlined clauses.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attachment: MAP_final.xlsx)
